representation: Consolidated MODRISS method content mapped to SPEM 2.0

roleDefinitions.name: Application Engineer
responsibilities: Reviews generated code, completes application configuration, and fixes implementation gaps

roleDefinitions.name: Business Modeler
responsibilities: Leads CIM discovery and domain-model increments

roleDefinitions.name: Cloud Platform Engineer
responsibilities: Leads AWS PSM, generation, environments, and platform automation

roleDefinitions.name: Delivery Lead
responsibilities: Maintains the integrated process run, dependency board, risks, cadence, and impediment escalation

roleDefinitions.name: Domain Expert
responsibilities: Validates business language, rules, and operational fit

roleDefinitions.name: FinOps and Cost Analyst
responsibilities: Owns cost hypotheses, budgets, allocation, anomaly thresholds, and cost feedback

roleDefinitions.name: Method Engineer
responsibilities: Tailors and evolves the situational method and its process assets

roleDefinitions.name: Process Reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews gates, evidence, decisions, and method improvement

roleDefinitions.name: Product Owner
responsibilities: Owns product outcomes, priority, release scope, and acceptance decisions

roleDefinitions.name: Quality Engineer
responsibilities: Owns verification strategy, evidence quality, and quality risks

roleDefinitions.name: Records and Data Steward
responsibilities: Owns retention, disposition, migration evidence, and lifecycle closure for records and data

roleDefinitions.name: Release Engineer
responsibilities: Owns release candidates, promotion, rollback, and deployment records

roleDefinitions.name: Requirements Engineer
responsibilities: Maintains requirements, acceptance criteria, and change impact evidence

roleDefinitions.name: Security Engineer
responsibilities: Owns security, privacy, threat, and exception evidence

roleDefinitions.name: Service Owner
responsibilities: Accepts operational readiness, SLOs, support ownership, and service outcomes

roleDefinitions.name: Solution Architect
responsibilities: Leads PIM architecture, contracts, integration, and cross-level decisions

roleDefinitions.name: Sponsor
responsibilities: Authorizes investment and resolves business-level escalations
Accepts continuation, redirection, and stop decisions

taskDefinitions.name: Review project structure and generated templates
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review project structure and generated templates
steps: Inspect template, source, configuration, documentation, and pipeline files in the artifact explorer.
Identify entry points, Lambda handlers, infrastructure resources, parameters, outputs, and generated deployment instructions.
Compare the generated structure with the PSM deployable slice and record missing or unexpected components.
exitCriteria: Project inventory and PSM-to-file trace are recorded
validationRules: Every deployable resource has an identifiable template or source owner

taskDefinitions.name: Establish source-control and release baseline
steps: Create a dedicated branch or repository according to team policy.
Commit the unmodified generated baseline with generator, PSM revision, and generation timestamp recorded.
Tag or otherwise identify the baseline so later refinements are reviewable.
exitCriteria: Baseline is versioned and reproducible
validationRules: No unreviewed local-only changes remain

taskDefinitions.name: Route structural gaps back to the PSM
taskDefinitions.purpose: Route structural gaps back to the PSM
steps: Classify each gap as a PSM modeling defect, generator limitation, or legitimate implementation refinement.
For missing resources, permissions, integrations, or policies, update and validate the PSM before regenerating artifacts.
Record the reason for any approved hand-maintained template extension.
exitCriteria: PSM feedback and local refinements have named owners
validationRules: Architecture decisions are not hidden only in generated files

taskDefinitions.name: Complete repository hygiene
steps: Add repository documentation, ownership, license, ignore rules, and contribution instructions required by the organization.
Confirm generated documentation names the service, supported environments, and deployment prerequisites.
Ensure build outputs and local credentials are excluded from source control.
exitCriteria: Repository can be safely shared and reviewed
validationRules: Repository contains no generated build output or credential material

taskDefinitions.name: Define parameter and environment contract
steps: List required parameters, outputs, domains, regions, account IDs, tags, feature flags, and external endpoints.
Provide validated values or references for development, test, staging, and production.
Document defaults, allowed ranges, and the owner for every environment-specific value.
entryCriteria: Deployment templates and runtime configuration are known
exitCriteria: All environment values have a documented source and owner
validationRules: Production values are not copied into non-production configuration

taskDefinitions.name: Configure secret references and encryption
steps: Replace inline credentials, tokens, and sensitive defaults with approved secret-manager or parameter-store references.
Verify encryption keys, rotation expectations, and access paths for each secret or protected data store.
Document bootstrap steps that create secrets before deployment.
exitCriteria: Secrets are externalized and bootstrap steps are reproducible
validationRules: No secret value is committed to source control or template defaults

taskDefinitions.name: Review IAM and deployment permissions
steps: Review execution roles, resource policies, and CI/CD identities against least-privilege requirements.
Separate deployment permissions from application runtime permissions.
Record exceptions, approval owners, and expiration dates for elevated access.
entryCriteria: Infrastructure and delivery identities are defined
exitCriteria: Required permissions are approved and bounded
validationRules: No wildcard permission remains without documented justification

taskDefinitions.name: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline
taskDefinitions.purpose: Implement repeatable build and deployment pipeline
steps: Configure the approved CI/CD workflow to restore dependencies, build, package, validate, and deploy the artifact.
Pin or record runtime, build-image, and dependency-resolution versions.
Require review and controlled promotion between environments.
entryCriteria: Environment contract and deployment identities are available
exitCriteria: A pipeline can produce a uniquely identifiable release candidate
validationRules: Build and deploy steps do not depend on a developer workstation

taskDefinitions.name: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run reproducible build and infrastructure validation
steps: Build and package the project using the delivery pipeline.
Run the project's infrastructure/template validation and capture the results.
Verify generated deployment artifacts match the tagged source revision.
exitCriteria: Build and template validation evidence is retained
validationRules: Build succeeds from a clean environment

taskDefinitions.name: Assess dependencies and security findings
steps: Run approved dependency, secret, and infrastructure security scans.
Triage findings by severity and exploitability; fix blockers or obtain time-bound risk acceptance.
Verify logging, encryption, retention, and data-handling controls meet the PSM intent.
exitCriteria: Security findings are resolved or formally accepted
validationRules: No unresolved critical finding proceeds without explicit risk acceptance

taskDefinitions.name: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests
taskDefinitions.purpose: Deploy to staging and execute acceptance tests
steps: Deploy the exact candidate through the pipeline to a controlled non-production environment.
Execute smoke, integration, contract, and business acceptance tests for the deployable slice.
Record test data constraints, results, defects, and any accepted deviations.
exitCriteria: Acceptance evidence covers critical user and integration paths
validationRules: Tests target the deployed candidate as well as local code

taskDefinitions.name: Verify observability and operational signals
steps: Confirm logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, and alarms are emitted for critical paths.
Trigger representative failure and recovery scenarios to verify alert routing and diagnostic context.
Set practical thresholds and identify the team that responds to each alert.
exitCriteria: Critical operational signals and alert ownership are verified
validationRules: An operator can detect and diagnose a failed critical path

taskDefinitions.name: Create release, rollback, and communication plan
taskDefinitions.purpose: Create release, rollback, and communication plan
steps: Define release scope, version, deployment sequence, approvals, maintenance window, and stakeholder communications.
Document rollback triggers, steps, data considerations, decision owner, and expected recovery time.
Rehearse rollback or recovery in non-production when the change affects data, interfaces, or critical availability.
exitCriteria: Release and rollback plan are approved by accountable owners
validationRules: Rollback does not rely on undocumented manual knowledge

taskDefinitions.name: Obtain production readiness approval
steps: Review release scope, risk, verification evidence, security findings, operational readiness, and rollback posture.
Capture go/no-go decision, approvers, constraints, and follow-up actions.
Confirm support and business stakeholders understand the release window and success criteria.
entryCriteria: Release plan and evidence are available
exitCriteria: Go/no-go decision is recorded
validationRules: Production deployment has an accountable approver

taskDefinitions.name: Complete operations handover
steps: Publish runbooks for deployment, rollback, common incidents, access requests, and escalation.
Assign service ownership, on-call coverage, dashboards, alerts, service objectives, and support contacts.
Transfer repository, pipeline, and environment access according to the operating model.
exitCriteria: Operations team can support the deployed service
validationRules: Runbooks identify owners and escalation paths

taskDefinitions.name: Execute production validation and close release
taskDefinitions.purpose: Execute production validation and close release
steps: Deploy the approved release candidate using the documented pipeline and plan.
Perform post-deployment smoke checks, monitor health signals, and confirm business and technical success criteria.
Close the release or invoke rollback; record lessons and feed recurring issues to the PSM or generator backlog.
exitCriteria: Production outcome and follow-up actions are recorded
validationRules: Production health is checked before the release is closed

taskDefinitions.name: Create CIM model root
steps: Create or verify CIMModel with domainName and businessScope.
Set organizationName, modelingDate, and language.
Apply lifecycle status and annotation conventions on the root.
entryCriteria: Project created or existing CIM opened for a new increment
exitCriteria: CIMModel root with domainName exists

taskDefinitions.name: Establish shared model contract and evidence conventions
taskDefinitions.purpose: Establish shared model contract and evidence conventions
steps: Apply the shared identity, annotation, traceability, expression, and lifecycle conventions used by every CIM element.
Set the evidence convention for source references, review status, and model-level provenance.
Confirm that shared support concepts are handled by inspectors and readiness records rather than mistaken for business concepts.
exitCriteria: Shared model contract and evidence convention are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Plan capability slice
steps: Select one capability or bounded-context candidate from the modeling backlog.
Record slice objective, scope boundaries, assumptions, and definition of done.
Identify the validation gate and review participants for the cycle.
exitCriteria: Capability-slice scope and definition of done are agreed

taskDefinitions.name: Define business goals and KPIs
steps: Capture BusinessGoal elements with success criteria.
Define measurable KPIs linked to each goal.
exitCriteria: At least one goal with linked KPI
validationRules: CIM-GOAL-001
CIM-KPI-001

taskDefinitions.name: Identify stakeholders
steps: Register stakeholders and their concerns linked to goals.
exitCriteria: Stakeholders identified for primary outcomes

taskDefinitions.name: Model actors and roles
steps: Model human and system Actor elements with trust levels.
Define Role elements and link to actors.
exitCriteria: Actors exist for primary user journeys

taskDefinitions.name: Register external systems
steps: Register ExternalSystem actors at domain boundaries.
exitCriteria: External integrations at boundaries identified

taskDefinitions.name: Map business capabilities
steps: Create BusinessCapability elements linked to goals.
Set criticality for each capability in the increment slice.
exitCriteria: Capabilities cover core value streams for slice

taskDefinitions.name: Record capability dependencies
steps: Model CapabilityDependency relationships between capabilities.
exitCriteria: Dependencies documented for slice

taskDefinitions.name: Define domain glossary
steps: Define UbiquitousLanguageTerm entries with definitions and examples.
Link terms to capabilities where helpful.
Resolve naming conflicts before entity modeling.
exitCriteria: Glossary covers core domain nouns for slice

taskDefinitions.name: Define data classifications
steps: Create DataClassification elements with confidentiality levels.
exitCriteria: Classifications cover sensitive categories

taskDefinitions.name: Create information items
steps: Create InformationItem elements for each planned entity attribute group.
Set identifiability and data kind on each item.
exitCriteria: Information items exist for planned entities
validationRules: CIM-ENTITY-001

taskDefinitions.name: Model domain entities
steps: Create DomainEntity elements referencing primary InformationItem identity.
Define lifecycle states and business invariants per entity.
exitCriteria: Core entities for slice modeled
validationRules: CIM-ENTITY-001

taskDefinitions.name: Model value objects and relationships
steps: Add ValueObject elements for descriptive data.
Model DomainRelationship elements between concepts.
exitCriteria: Relationships and VOs complete for slice
validationRules: CIM-RELATIONSHIP-001

taskDefinitions.name: Model commands and outcomes
steps: Create Command elements with actors and target capabilities.
Define CommandOutcome and link expected/rejection events.
exitCriteria: Commands cover primary write use cases

taskDefinitions.name: Model queries
steps: Create Query elements linked to actors and information items.
Set freshness requirements per query.
exitCriteria: Queries cover primary read use cases

taskDefinitions.name: Model events, errors, and conditions
steps: Create BusinessEvent elements emitted by commands or external systems.
Define BusinessError and Condition elements guarding behavior.
exitCriteria: Event vocabulary covers slice workflows

taskDefinitions.name: Define aggregate candidates
steps: Create AggregateCandidate groupings with handled commands and emitted events.
Document consistency and interaction expectations.
exitCriteria: Aggregates align with command/event ownership

taskDefinitions.name: Model business processes
steps: Create BusinessProcess with step hierarchy and transitions.
Connect steps to modeled commands, queries, events, and policies.
exitCriteria: Key processes orchestrate modeled behavior

taskDefinitions.name: Define policies and decision tables
steps: Create Policy elements guarding commands, events, and processes.
Model DecisionTable with DecisionRule rows for branching logic.
exitCriteria: Policies linked to behavior elements

taskDefinitions.name: Synthesize bounded contexts
steps: Group capabilities, entities, CQRS, events, and policies into contexts.
Validate memberships reference concrete modeled elements.
exitCriteria: Contexts have non-empty memberships

taskDefinitions.name: Formalize requirements
steps: Create Requirement elements with constrains links to domain and behavior.
Add AcceptanceCriterion per requirement.
exitCriteria: Requirements trace to goals and model elements

taskDefinitions.name: Apply governance constraints
steps: Record security, privacy, and compliance constraints on actors and information items.
exitCriteria: Governance constraints linked to targets

taskDefinitions.name: Record transformation metadata
steps: Record Risk, Assumption, and Hotspot elements on model hotspots.
Define TransformationProfile for CIM→PIM with manual decisions.
exitCriteria: Transformation profile ready for ETL

taskDefinitions.name: Complete trace and readiness
steps: Build TraceModel links across goals, requirements, and domain.
Complete ProductionReadinessAssessment and resolve findings.
exitCriteria: CIM EVL passes; readiness approved
validationRules: cim-semantic-validation

taskDefinitions.name: Review and adapt CIM increment
steps: Review slice outcomes against goals, KPIs, and acceptance criteria.
Record accepted scope, deferred work, and stakeholder feedback.
Create improvement actions and backlog adjustments for the next engine cycle.
entryCriteria: CIM EVL passes or all blocking findings are dispositioned
exitCriteria: Increment accepted or rework loop selected; improvement actions captured

taskDefinitions.name: Plan the vertical increment
steps: Select scope from the ordered product backlog.
Define outcome, acceptance criteria, dependencies, risks, and expected model/artifact evidence.
Assign scope items to owning teams and establish the increment ledger.
exitCriteria: Increment scope, owners, acceptance evidence, and dependencies are agreed
validationRules: The slice is small enough to inspect end-to-end and large enough to demonstrate a user or operational outcome
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Plan the vertical increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the CIM increment
steps: Execute the CIM process for the selected capability slice.
Record semantic decisions, assumptions, trace links, readiness findings, and accepted CIM revision.
Return unresolved cross-team or product decisions to the integrated decision register.
exitCriteria: CIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Assistant-applied model changes pass structural Ecore/EMF conformance; semantic validation remains an explicit user/model validation workflow
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the CIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation
steps: Pin the source CIM revision and transformation profile.
Run the transformation and inspect report, trace links, assumptions, and manual decisions.
Accept, reject, or route each material decision and record the target PIM revision.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every generated target scope item is traceable to a source or explicit transformation decision
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect CIM-to-PIM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the PIM increment
steps: Execute the PIM process for the transformed slice.
Review contracts, data access, integration, policy, platform mapping, and operational assumptions.
Record accepted PIM revision and open platform decisions.
exitCriteria: PIM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: Generated PIM is treated as scaffolding until the solution architect accepts material decisions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the PIM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation
steps: Pin the source PIM revision and AWS mapping profile.
Run the transformation and inspect resource mappings, assumptions, security implications, and trace links.
Record accepted target PSM revision or route mapping gaps back to PIM.
exitCriteria: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every deployable PIM scope item has an accepted AWS mapping or a documented exception
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute and inspect PIM-to-PSM transformation decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run the PSM increment
steps: Execute the AWS PSM process for the transformed slice.
Review resource relationships, IAM, networking, data, eventing, APIs, workflows, and operational views.
Record accepted PSM revision and unresolved deployment risks.
exitCriteria: PSM gate evidence is accepted or explicitly reworked
validationRules: AWS platform choices are traceable to accepted PIM intent or explicit platform decisions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run the PSM increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline
taskDefinitions.purpose: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline
steps: Pin PSM revision, generator version, templates, and environment profile.
Generate application, infrastructure, configuration, tests, and documentation artifacts.
Record the generation manifest and route structural gaps to PSM or generator ownership.
exitCriteria: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline evidence is recorded
validationRules: The generated baseline is reproducible from recorded inputs and contains no secret material
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Generate and fingerprint the artifact baseline decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment
taskDefinitions.purpose: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment
steps: Execute the artifact deployment-readiness process for the generated candidate.
Review verification, security, rollback, operational, and acceptance evidence.
Record increment outcome, open findings, deferred scope, and feedback loops for the next cycle.
exitCriteria: Increment is accepted, explicitly deferred, or returned through a named rework loop
validationRules: No blocking finding is silently closed; risk acceptance is explicit, owned, time-bound, and traceable
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Run artifact readiness and accept the increment decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define product outcomes and success measures
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define product outcomes and success measures
steps: State the user or mission problem and desired outcomes.
Define measurable product, operational, security, and quality outcomes.
Record assumptions, constraints, non-goals, and the first release hypothesis.
exitCriteria: Outcome measures and non-goals are accepted by stakeholders
validationRules: Every initial scope item is connected to an outcome or mandatory constraint
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define product outcomes and success measures decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis
taskDefinitions.purpose: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis
steps: Identify the smallest useful vertical capability slice.
Define acceptance signals and the evidence needed to call it usable.
Record unresolved assumptions as owned decisions rather than hidden risks.
exitCriteria: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis evidence is recorded
validationRules: The first slice crosses the required lifecycle boundary and has observable acceptance evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Establish the initial release and increment hypothesis decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assess context and method risks
steps: Assess criticality, regulatory obligations, novelty, uncertainty, team distribution, system size, and delivery cadence.
Select the required CIM, PIM, PSM, artifact, and lifecycle activities.
Record excluded, combined, or delegated activities with rationale and compensating evidence.
exitCriteria: Assess context and method risks evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every tailoring decision names its context, consequence, owner, and review point
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assess context and method risks decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done
steps: Define entry and exit evidence for model slices, transformations, release candidates, and operations.
Define which findings are blocking and how time-bound risk acceptance works.
Publish the profile version used by the process run.
exitCriteria: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done evidence is recorded
validationRules: A task cannot be accepted solely because activity occurred; required evidence and gate criteria are explicit
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define the tailored Definition of Ready and Done decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define team ownership and interfaces
steps: Partition work by bounded capability, service, platform concern, or lifecycle responsibility.
Assign model ownership, repository ownership, decision rights, and backup owners.
Define interface contracts and the shared dependency board.
exitCriteria: Define team ownership and interfaces evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every owned model scope has one accountable owner and a named integration path
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define team ownership and interfaces decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths
taskDefinitions.purpose: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths
steps: Set local team syncs, cross-team integration reviews, increment reviews, release reviews, and retrospectives.
Define escalation thresholds for aging dependencies, blocking findings, and conflicting model ownership.
Define how concurrent model edits are merged, reviewed, and reconciled.
exitCriteria: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths evidence is recorded
validationRules: Coordination events produce decisions, dependency status, and evidence links
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Set coordination cadence and escalation paths decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define quality and security control objectives
taskDefinitions.purpose: Define quality and security control objectives
steps: Identify privacy, threat, compliance, resilience, performance, accessibility, and audit obligations.
Map control objectives to model evidence, generated artifact evidence, and explicit human decisions.
Set severity and blocking policies.
exitCriteria: Define quality and security control objectives evidence is recorded
validationRules: Critical controls have an accountable owner and verification evidence path
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define quality and security control objectives decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define operational and release strategy
steps: Define environments, support ownership, SLO hypotheses, observability expectations, rollback posture, and release cadence.
Identify data migration, compatibility, and progressive-delivery constraints.
Record the initial release decision policy.
exitCriteria: Define operational and release strategy evidence is recorded
validationRules: The release strategy names promotion, rollback, and post-deployment validation evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Define operational and release strategy decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assemble the release candidate
steps: Select accepted increments and compatible model/artifact revisions.
Resolve cross-team dependency and compatibility checks.
Create the release record with exact inputs and promotion sequence.
exitCriteria: Assemble the release candidate evidence is recorded
validationRules: Every release scope item maps to an accepted increment and exact artifact identity
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assemble the release candidate decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria
steps: Inspect readiness assessments, validation results, security exceptions, rollback plan, operational runbooks, and approvals.
Confirm open blockers are zero or explicitly accepted under the tailored method profile.
Record the go/no-go decision and decision owners.
exitCriteria: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria evidence is recorded
validationRules: Go/no-go is evidence-based and not inferred from task completion
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review release evidence and go/no-go criteria decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Deploy and validate progressively
steps: Deploy the exact candidate to the approved environment sequence.
Run smoke, functional, security, data, observability, and compatibility checks.
Compare observed outcomes with release acceptance signals and stop or roll back on threshold breach.
exitCriteria: Deploy and validate progressively evidence is recorded
validationRules: Promotion evidence identifies candidate, environment, timestamp, operator, and observed result
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Deploy and validate progressively decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal
steps: Verify dashboards, alerts, runbooks, escalation paths, support ownership, and recovery access.
Confirm rollback and data-recovery actions are usable for the release.
Accept operational ownership or return the release to rework.
exitCriteria: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational acceptance names an accountable service owner and recovery evidence
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Complete handover and rollback rehearsal decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review release outcome and update roadmap
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review release outcome and update roadmap
steps: Compare product and operational outcomes with the release hypothesis.
Accept outcomes, revise priorities, and create follow-up increments for gaps.
Record decisions and changes to scope, measures, and assumptions.
exitCriteria: Review release outcome and update roadmap evidence is recorded
validationRules: Outcome learning changes a backlog, product decision, or explicitly confirms the hypothesis
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review release outcome and update roadmap decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes
taskDefinitions.purpose: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes
steps: Inspect service levels, errors, cost, security signals, usage, and product outcome measures.
Compare observations with the service and product hypotheses.
Create improvement or change items with evidence and owners.
exitCriteria: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes evidence is recorded
validationRules: Operational decisions are based on identified evidence and thresholds
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Review SLOs, telemetry, and product outcomes decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Manage incidents and recovery
steps: Triage impact, stabilize service, communicate status, and execute approved recovery actions.
Record incident timeline, affected scope, decisions, and evidence.
Open problem, security, or change work for systemic causes.
exitCriteria: Manage incidents and recovery evidence is recorded
validationRules: Recovery and customer impact are recorded before closure
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Manage incidents and recovery decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Perform problem and risk learning
steps: Analyze contributing causes across requirements, models, transformation, generation, deployment, and operation.
Update controls, tests, model patterns, process guidance, or method profile as appropriate.
Review changes at the next increment or release boundary.
exitCriteria: Perform problem and risk learning evidence is recorded
validationRules: The corrective action is routed to the earliest responsible source rather than only patched downstream
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Perform problem and risk learning decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Assess and propagate a change
steps: Classify the change as product, domain, architecture, platform, artifact, operational, or retirement scope.
Use traces and dependency ownership to identify impacted downstream levels and teams.
Re-enter the smallest affected process stage, regenerate or redeploy as required, and preserve compatibility evidence.
exitCriteria: Assess and propagate a change evidence is recorded
validationRules: The change record identifies source revision, impacted levels, downstream evidence, and acceptance decision
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Assess and propagate a change decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics
taskDefinitions.purpose: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics
steps: Review flow time, rework, trace coverage, blockers, dependency age, escaped defects, and product outcomes.
Look for systemic queues, missing work products, invalid gates, and coordination failures.
Approve bounded method changes and record their expected effect.
exitCriteria: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics evidence is recorded
validationRules: Metrics lead to inspectable improvement experiments rather than individual performance rankings
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Inspect flow, quality, and coordination metrics decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Approve retirement scope and plan
steps: Confirm business, technical, legal, security, and operational reasons for retirement.
Define replacement, user communication, compatibility, rollback, and exit criteria.
Assign owners and schedule decision checkpoints.
exitCriteria: Approve retirement scope and plan evidence is recorded
validationRules: The plan identifies affected stakeholders, dependencies, and irreversible actions
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Approve retirement scope and plan decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Execute migration and data disposition
steps: Execute migration, archival, retention, deletion, or export according to approved policy.
Validate completeness, confidentiality, integrity, and recoverability where required.
Record final data and integration evidence.
exitCriteria: Execute migration and data disposition evidence is recorded
validationRules: No data or integration is silently abandoned
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Execute migration and data disposition decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Decommission service and access
steps: Disable traffic, scheduled work, credentials, access paths, alerts, and environments in the approved order.
Verify replacement ownership and customer communication.
Retain required source, model, trace, release, incident, and decision records.
exitCriteria: Decommission service and access evidence is recorded
validationRules: Decommission evidence covers runtime, data, access, cost, and support surfaces
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Decommission service and access decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Complete closure review
steps: Confirm retirement exit criteria and records are complete.
Review product, architecture, operational, and method outcomes.
Publish reusable patterns, risks, and method changes for future projects.
exitCriteria: Complete closure review evidence is recorded
validationRules: Closure identifies retained evidence, unresolved obligations, and accountable custodians
taskDefinitions.progressEvidence: Complete closure review decision, evidence links, owner, and status are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Plan service slice
steps: Select one service slice traced to CIM goals, bounded contexts, and behavior.
Record scope boundaries, architectural risks, manual transform decisions, and definition of done.
Confirm the expected PIM EVL gate and review participants for the cycle.
entryCriteria: CIM transform complete, prior PIM increment selected, or greenfield PIM
exitCriteria: Service-slice scope and definition of done are agreed

taskDefinitions.name: Create PIM model root
steps: Create or verify PIMModel with domain linkage to CIM source.
Set modeling date, lifecycle status, and annotation conventions.
exitCriteria: PIMModel root exists

taskDefinitions.name: Set architecture posture
steps: Configure ImplementationProfile with serverless posture and platform assumptions.
Select ArchitectureStyle and document key architectural decisions.
exitCriteria: Architecture style and profile configured

taskDefinitions.name: Establish shared model contract and evidence conventions
taskDefinitions.purpose: Establish shared model contract and evidence conventions
steps: Apply shared identity, annotation, traceability, expression, and lifecycle conventions across PIM elements.
Record the revision, transformation provenance, and review-state convention for the service slice.
Keep support concepts in inspectors and readiness evidence instead of exposing them as false deployable architecture nodes.
exitCriteria: Shared model contract and evidence convention are recorded

taskDefinitions.name: Define serverless services
steps: Create ServerlessService elements aligned to CIM bounded contexts.
Set boundary type and ownership scope per service.
exitCriteria: Services defined for increment slice

taskDefinitions.name: Assign element memberships
steps: Create ServiceElementMembership links from services to planned elements.
Set OwnershipKind for each membership.
exitCriteria: Memberships cover deployable boundaries

taskDefinitions.name: Define schemas and fields
steps: Create Schema elements with fields and enum literals.
Set schema kind and field types aligned to CIM information items.
exitCriteria: Schemas cover API and message payloads

taskDefinitions.name: Model event types and envelopes
steps: Define EventType and EventEnvelope elements from CIM events.
Apply validation constraints and compatibility rules.
exitCriteria: Event contracts aligned with CIM behavior surface

taskDefinitions.name: Model data stores and models
steps: Create DataStore and ObjectStore elements per service.
Define DataModel and DataField structures from CIM entities.
exitCriteria: Stores and models cover domain data

taskDefinitions.name: Define access patterns and indexes

guidance.name: Environment parity with explicit differences
guidance.text: Keep development, test, staging, and production configuration structurally equivalent. Record intentional differences as parameters or approved environment exceptions.

guidance.name: Evidence before promotion
guidance.text: Promotion requires reproducible build, validation, test, and security evidence for the exact release candidate.

guidance.name: Generated output is a controlled baseline
guidance.text: Treat generated files as a PSM-derived baseline: review every generated change, commit it to source control, and feed structural defects back to the PSM instead of repeatedly patching generated output.

guidance.name: No secrets in artifacts
guidance.text: Store secret values only in the approved secret manager or CI/CD secret store; generated templates and repositories contain references, never secret material.

guidance.name: Rehearse recovery
guidance.text: A release is not ready until rollback, data protection, alerting, and ownership are demonstrably usable by the on-call team.

guidance.name: Ubiquitous language first (Evans)
guidance.text: Agree domain vocabulary before modeling entities. Renaming later is expensive. Use glossary tasks early.

guidance.name: Event storming surface (Brandolini)
guidance.text: Model commands, queries, and events on a behavior surface linked to actors and capabilities before aggregates.

guidance.name: Goal-Question-Metric (Basili)
guidance.text: Anchor every modeling increment with measurable business goals before structural or behavioral elements.

guidance.name: Thin capability slices
guidance.text: Run CIM as an empirical increment cycle: select one valuable capability slice, model only enough breadth to satisfy the slice definition of done, review, then adapt the backlog.

guidance.name: Information before entity (CIM-ENTITY-001)
guidance.text: Create InformationItem elements before DomainEntity. Primary identity must reference an information item.

guidance.name: Computation-independent intent
guidance.text: CIM captures business meaning without platform or implementation choices. Defer technology decisions to PIM/PSM.

guidance.name: Twin Peaks requirements (Nuseibeh)
guidance.text: Backfill formal requirements after domain structure exists. Use engine rework loops when requirements expose gaps.

guidance.name: Empirical process control
guidance.text: Plan a small vertical slice, inspect executable model evidence at each gate, and adapt the backlog after artifact review.

guidance.name: Human-in-the-loop transforms
guidance.text: ETL and M2T are assistive. ManualDecision and readiness gates block promotion when automation is uncertain.

guidance.name: Thin vertical increments
guidance.text: Deliver one capability slice through CIM → PIM → PSM → artifact readiness per engine revolution. The engine repeats inside release, operations, and retirement lifecycle governance; avoid big-bang modeling.

guidance.name: MF-01 — Opportunity and feasibility
guidance.description: A project can commit to a solution before value, feasibility, constraints, and alternatives are understood. Result: The endeavor is pursued, explored, redirected, or stopped with explicit evidence.
guidance.initialContext: A problem, opportunity, or change proposal exists.
guidance.resultContext: The endeavor is pursued, explored, redirected, or stopped with explicit evidence.

guidance.name: MF-02 — Serverless suitability, cost, risk, and provider decision
guidance.description: Serverless and provider commitments can be made without workload, cost, risk, or exit analysis. Result: A serverless/hybrid/non-serverless and provider decision or bounded experiment is authorized.
guidance.initialContext: Business outcomes, constraints, and candidate workload are known enough to compare alternatives.
guidance.resultContext: A serverless/hybrid/non-serverless and provider decision or bounded experiment is authorized.

guidance.name: MF-03 — Situational method tailoring
guidance.description: One fixed process either overburdens a project or omits necessary controls. Result: A versioned method profile selects content, evidence depth, roles, and review triggers.
guidance.initialContext: Product, risk, team, platform, compliance, and delivery factors are assessable.
guidance.resultContext: A versioned method profile selects content, evidence depth, roles, and review triggers.

guidance.name: MF-04 — Product, release, and increment framing
guidance.description: Modeling can become an end in itself without a bounded outcome and acceptance evidence. Result: A valuable vertical slice is ready with owners, risks, dependencies, and evidence.
guidance.initialContext: An authorized product and method profile exist.
guidance.resultContext: A valuable vertical slice is ready with owners, risks, dependencies, and evidence.

guidance.name: MF-05 — Event-driven domain discovery and CIM modeling
guidance.description: Business meaning can be lost if software/provider structure is chosen before domain and requirement understanding. Result: An accepted computation-independent model expresses intent, behavior, policy, and governance.
guidance.initialContext: An increment is ready and domain participants/sources are available.
guidance.resultContext: An accepted computation-independent model expresses intent, behavior, policy, and governance.

guidance.name: MF-06 — CIM assurance and readiness
guidance.description: An incomplete or inconsistent CIM can propagate false certainty downstream. Result: The revision is accepted, reworked, or deferred with trace and findings.
guidance.initialContext: A candidate CIM revision and acceptance context exist.
guidance.resultContext: The revision is accepted, reworked, or deferred with trace and findings.

guidance.name: MF-07 — CIM to PIM transformation and reconciliation
guidance.description: Automated refinement can overwrite human decisions or hide unresolved mappings. Result: A traceable PIM draft is merged or conflicts/manual decisions are explicit.
guidance.initialContext: An accepted CIM and transformation profile exist.
guidance.resultContext: A traceable PIM draft is merged or conflicts/manual decisions are explicit.
guidance.selection: required when using the MODRISS transform

guidance.name: MF-08 — Platform-independent serverless architecture
guidance.description: Serverless architecture needs explicit provider-independent services, contracts, state, integration, workflow, security, and operability. Result: An accepted provider-independent architecture is ready for capability mapping.
guidance.initialContext: A PIM draft and authoritative CIM/requirements trace exist.
guidance.resultContext: An accepted provider-independent architecture is ready for capability mapping.

guidance.name: MF-09 — PIM to PSM transformation and reconciliation
guidance.description: Provider mapping can silently introduce unsafe defaults or lose refinements. Result: A traceable PSM draft is merged and mapping gaps/conflicts are explicit.
guidance.initialContext: An accepted PIM and chosen supported provider profile exist.
guidance.resultContext: A traceable PSM draft is merged and mapping gaps/conflicts are explicit.

guidance.name: MF-10 — AWS PSM refinement and assurance
guidance.description: Generated provider resources require explicit security, networking, quota, observability, recovery, cost, and deployment decisions. Result: An accepted AWS PSM is ready for reproducible generation.
guidance.initialContext: A reconciled AWS PSM draft and PIM trace exist.
guidance.resultContext: An accepted AWS PSM is ready for reproducible generation.

guidance.name: MF-11 — Reproducible model-to-text generation
guidance.description: Generated output cannot be trusted or reproduced without exact source, template, configuration, and manifest provenance. Result: A generated-draft baseline and traceable manifest exist.
guidance.initialContext: An accepted PSM revision and generator profile exist.
guidance.resultContext: A generated-draft baseline and traceable manifest exist.

guidance.name: MF-12 — Artifact completion and test in the small
guidance.description: Generated scaffolds can be mistaken for complete, correct software. Result: Business logic and extensions are complete and component evidence is available.
guidance.initialContext: A generated baseline, trace, and manual-action report exist.
guidance.resultContext: Business logic and extensions are complete and component evidence is available.

guidance.name: MF-13 — Test in the large and release qualification
guidance.description: Locally correct functions and templates may fail as an integrated serverless service. Result: System, acceptance, NFR, security, resilience, recovery, and operational evidence support a release decision.
guidance.initialContext: A candidate baseline can be deployed to a representative non-production environment.
guidance.resultContext: System, acceptance, NFR, security, resilience, recovery, and operational evidence support a release decision.

guidance.name: MF-14 — Progressive CI/CD and transition
guidance.description: A technically valid candidate can still fail during promotion or handover. Result: The release is progressively promoted, observed, recorded, and accepted for operation.
guidance.initialContext: An immutable qualified candidate and recovery plan exist.
guidance.resultContext: The release is progressively promoted, observed, recorded, and accepted for operation.

guidance.name: MF-15 — Operate, observe, control cost, and learn
guidance.description: A deployed serverless service needs operational ownership and feedback to remain valuable, reliable, secure, and economical. Result: Service/product outcomes, SLOs, risk, security, and cost are controlled and feed prioritized change.
guidance.initialContext: A release has operational ownership and telemetry.
guidance.resultContext: Service/product outcomes, SLOs, risk, security, and cost are controlled and feed prioritized change.

guidance.name: MF-16 — Incident, problem, and controlled change propagation
guidance.description: Emergency or evolutionary changes can diverge models, generators, code, and the running service. Result: Service is restored where necessary and change is routed to the earliest authoritative source and re-evidenced.
guidance.initialContext: An incident, finding, dependency, or requested change exists.
guidance.resultContext: Service is restored where necessary and change is routed to the earliest authoritative source and re-evidenced.

guidance.name: MF-17 — Retirement, migration, and closure
guidance.description: A service can be switched off while data, consumers, access, resources, costs, or legal obligations remain. Result: Users, data, integrations, access, resources, cost, and evidence are migrated or closed and accepted.
guidance.initialContext: A retirement/replacement trigger and accountable product/service owners exist.
guidance.resultContext: Users, data, integrations, access, resources, cost, and evidence are migrated or closed and accepted.

guidance.name: UF-01 — Integrated management, assurance, and evidence
guidance.description: Lifecycle tasks become disconnected without continuous planning, risk, quality, security, change, trace, and evidence management. Result: Decisions, dependencies, risks, findings, revisions, evidence, and improvement remain controlled throughout the run.
guidance.resultContext: Decisions, dependencies, risks, findings, revisions, evidence, and improvement remain controlled throughout the run.
guidance.selection: continuous and required; depth is tailored

guidance.name: Contracts decouple producers
guidance.text: Define schemas and event types before wiring functions and routes. Contracts are the integration currency.

guidance.name: Access patterns drive stores
guidance.text: Model read/write access patterns from CIM queries/commands before choosing store topology.

guidance.name: Generated PIM is a draft
guidance.text: Treat CIM→PIM output as architectural scaffolding. Every generated service slice must pass through framing, refinement, readiness, and review before PIM→PSM.

guidance.name: Policy attachment discipline
guidance.text: Attach resilience, observability, and compliance policies to concrete PolicyTarget elements, not free-floating rules.

guidance.name: Readiness is part of delivery
guidance.text: Platform mapping and EVL validation are not after-the-fact audits. They are the review gate of each service-slice cycle.

guidance.name: Service as deployable boundary
guidance.text: Align ServerlessService boundaries to CIM bounded contexts. One increment typically maps to one service slice.

guidance.name: Deployable slice discipline
guidance.text: A PSM increment is done only when AWS wiring, least-privilege posture, observability, traceability, and artifact-generation readiness are reviewed together.

guidance.name: Generated PSM is a draft
guidance.text: Treat PIM→PSM output as AWS scaffolding. Refine IAM, networking, resource settings, integration views, and readiness before M2T generation.

guidance.name: Integration views for traceability
guidance.text: Relationship views denormalize cross-resource wiring for M2T and human review, create them before M2T generation.

guidance.name: Least-privilege IAM
guidance.text: Security baseline before compute. Lambda permissions and resource policies reference roles from the baseline.

guidance.name: SAM stack containment
guidance.text: Most AWS resources live under SamStack. Establish stack scaffolding before resource provisioning tasks.

processComponents.name: Full Software Lifecycle with CIM → PIM → PSM

repeatableActivities.name: Release Cycle
repeatableActivities.guidance: While the accepted release remains in operation, roadmap demand and operational evidence initiate a later release at Phase 1. Phase 4 is entered only through an authorized retirement decision.
